_readme: Japanese search terms mapped straight to the English wording this index uses,
bypassing the translation model for words it gets wrong.
Matching is on the WHOLE query, trimmed — not substrings. A single kanji recurs
inside unrelated words, and rewriting 縄 wherever it appeared would turn 沖縄
(Okinawa) into 'rope'. A search query is usually the bare term anyway.
Add a term when a Japanese search returns something unrelated: check what the
translator produced (the /api/v1/search response reports it as 'searched_as'),
and if that is the problem, map the term here. Put the English wording the
catalogue actually uses — grep enriched_products.db if unsure.
The entries below are what sugoi-v4 romanises rather than translates. It reads
和室 as 'Wamuro' — not even the right reading — where the ONNX backend managed
'Japanese-style room'. Loanwords that romanise correctly (着物 Kimono, 浴衣
Yukata, 布団 Futon) need no entry, because that IS the English word.
